messages.author: 0d5c994b344af3a8
messages.subject: Geocoding using RDSTK
parts:
Hello - Given Googles limit of 2500 queries per day, I am exploring using the RDSTK package which apparently does not have any limits. The street2coordinates gives me the latitude longitude given a address. 

However, I am facing problems when the package is not able to geocode a location (most likely because i have a non-existent address). For example, in the attached dataset, it is not able to geocode address for id = 19; and then gives me an error. 

Ideally, the code should return a NA for such addresses and move on to the next address (as ggmap's geocode function does). 

Thanks for your time. Anyone has experience using this package - in terms of accuracy of the lat/long?  

df <- read.csv("df.csv")

df$locationdesc <- paste(df$Address.Home.1, ", ", 
                         df$Address.Home.City, ", ", 
                         df$Address.Home.State, sep = " " , 
                         df$Postal)

library(RDSTK)

for (i in 1:nrow(df)) {
  results <- street2coordinates(address = df$locationdesc[i])
  df$hlong[i] <- results$longitude
  df$hlat[i] <- results$latitude
  rm(results, i)
}

The error I get is the following 

Error in df$hlong[i] <- results$longitude : replacement has length zero

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Geocoding using RDSTK
parts: Probably the easiest way to fix this would be to check the length of results and if it's 0, set to NA:

for (i in 1:nrow(df)) {
  results <- street2coordinates(address = df$locationdesc[i])

if(length(results) == 0){
      df$hlong[i] <- NA
      df$hlat[i] <- NA
  }else{

df$hlong[i] <- results$longitude
    df$hlat[i] <- results$latitude
 }
  rm(results, i)
}
(you'll need to check that results is actually length zero if the location is invalid and if not use another test, but you get the picture)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Geocoding using RDSTK
parts:
I think rather than just set the values to NA, it would be good to understand what is going on. After some basic debugging on #19 (calling getURL inside street2coordinates with verbose = TRUE), the API call is:

GET /street2coordinates/2085%20central%20ave%20

Or in other words, the "#" in the address is being interpreted as a comment character, so the address is incomplete when making the request. Entering ""2085 central ave 13, highland, CA 92346" results in:

{
  "2085 central ave 13,\thighland,\tCA\t92346": {
    "country_code3": "USA",
    "latitude": 34.135269,
    "country_name": "United States",
    "longitude": -117.217493,
    "street_address": "2085 Central Ave",
    "region": "CA",
    "confidence": 0.937,
    "street_number": "2085",
    "locality": "Highland",
    "street_name": "Central Ave",
    "fips_county": "06071",
    "country_code": "US"
  }

The street2coordinates() function is a pretty clunky implementation of accessing an API, but just an example of how debugging can pay off.

tl;dr - Sanitize your input by omitting "#", rather than setting setting the errors to NA.

Matt
